question: Which of the following diuretics is contraindicated in the presence of cardiac failure?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Mannitol" -> "osmotic diuretic" -> "increases intravascular volume" -> "may worsen cardiac failure" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Spironolactone" -> "potassium-sparing diuretic" -> "used in heart failure" -> "reduces mortality" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Furosemide" -> "loop diuretic" -> "commonly used in heart failure" -> "reduces fluid overload" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Hydrochlorothiazide" -> "thiazide diuretic" -> "not first-line for heart failure" -> "may be used cautiously" -> 70%
analysis: In the context of cardiac failure, the choice of diuretics is critical. Mannitol, an osmotic diuretic, increases intravascular volume, which can exacerbate heart failure symptoms by increasing preload. Therefore, it is contraindicated in patients with cardiac failure. On the other hand, spironolactone is beneficial in heart failure management due to its ability to block aldosterone, reducing mortality. Furosemide is a loop diuretic that is commonly used to manage fluid overload in heart failure patients. Hydrochlorothiazide is less effective in this context but is not outright contraindicated. Given this information, the diuretic that is contraindicated in the presence of cardiac failure is Mannitol.
